properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 957440
Incident Time: 2010-10-19 14:00:00
Nearest City: Seattle, WA
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 30 feet by 50 feet (area 1500 sq. ft.)
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0.04 gallons
AT APPROXIMATELY 0900 HRS. MARINA STAFF OBSERVED A THIN RAINBOW SHEEN IN THE WATER AT THE BOW OF THE 86' FISHING TENDER EIGIL B., EXTENDING 50' FROM IT, THEN POOLING IN AN AREA APPROXIMATELY 50' X 30'. MARINA STAFF MADE THE OBSERVATION FROM PIER A, WHILE THE VESSEL WAS ANCHORED ABOUT 150' AWAY. ANOTHER VESSEL, A U.S. NAVY TUG, SKENANDOA WAS ANCHORED NEARBY. PIER A IS A LARGE 300' LONG ELEVATED COMMERCIAL PIER. MARINA STAFF REPORTED THAT THE SHEEN APPEARED TO BE COMING FROM THE EIGIL B. AND NOT FROM THE SKENANDOA. MARINA STAFF HAD A REASONABLE SUSPICION TO BELIEVE THAT THE EIGIL B. WAS THE SOURCE OF THE SHEEN BUT COULD NOT VERIFY IT. MARINA OFFICE STAFF PHONED THE OWNER/OPERATOR AND INQUIRED ABOUT THE SHEEN. THEY STATED IN SUBSTANCE, ONLY, THAT THERE WAS ANOTHER VESSEL NEARBY. THEY STATED THAT THEY WERE UNDER WAY AND HAD DEPARTED THE MARINA. MARINA STAFF REPORTED THAT WHEN THE EIGIL B. DEPARTED THE MARINA, THE SHEEN WAS DISPERSED BY THE PROPELLER WASH AS THE VESSEL MOVED THROUGH IT. PHOTOS OF THE SHEEN WERE TAKEN BY MARINA STAFF.
